# SITREP Reconciliation

Use this whenever an Agent Pair or sibling orchestrator reports status after parallel work.

Teams have local context plus their last handoff. They often do not know what sibling teams shipped in parallel. The orchestrator must reconcile fresh reality and push back explicitly on stale claims.

## Standard SITREP input format

Ask teams to emit sitreps in this format:

```text
ROLE: <Planner | Implementer | Orchestrator Planner | Orchestrator Reviewer>
PHASE: SITREP
AUTHORITY: <report-only | read-only>
TASK_ID: <id or none>
DISPATCH_ID: <current dispatch id>
PARENT_DISPATCH_ID: <parent id or none>
EVIDENCE_TARGET: <E1 | E2 | E3 | E4>
FROM: <sender owner.role | orchestrator | operator>
TO: <recipient owner.role | orchestrator | operator>
CC: <boundary-adjacent owner.role; omit the line when none>
BUNDLE_ID: <bundle/lane id>
OWNER: <team/pair/agent>
BASE: <repo>@<branch>@<sha or unknown>
TARGET_BRANCH: <branch or none>
DISPATCH_REQUIRED_FOR_IMPL: <yes/no>
HUMAN_GATE_REQUIRED: <yes — decision | no | no — downstream: standing gate>
LIVE_VERIFY_REQUIRED: <yes/no + reason>
CEREMONY_TIER: <tiny | small | medium | large | production-risk>
CEREMONY_DOWNGRADE: <none | skipped steps + why safe>
FINAL_GIT_STATUS_SHORT: <paste exact output or unavailable — reason>

Current artifact:
<plan / PR / branch / commit / none>

Claims:
1. <claim> — evidence level <E0-E4> — source <file/test/PR/live>

Done:
- <completed items>

Not done:
- <remaining items>

Blocked:
- <blocker + owner of decision>

Scope drift risk:
- <none / risk>

Boundary contract status:
- Writes: <status>
- Reads: <status>
- Downstream consumer: <status>
- Target entity: <status>
- Proof: <status>

Tests / verification:
- <commands + result>

Next requested action:
<audit reconcile | proceed to plan | dispatch impl | review PR | fold review | merge gate | live verify | defer | human decision>
```

If a team sends a free-form sitrep, extract these fields and ask them to use the standard format next time.

`HUMAN_GATE_REQUIRED: yes` if and only if this relay's requested next transition cannot occur without a fresh operator decision; the operator may answer directly or route the ask onward — the field marks who is being asked, not who must answer. A `yes` names its ask in the annotation (`yes — <the decision>`); a bare `yes` is malformed and relay-lint warns on it; always annotate. Standing downstream gates are named only after `downstream:` or in prose; the field is free-form (`yes|no — <reason>`), not an enum. The field is a predicate re-evaluated at each relay, not a latch.

## Claim-evidence ladder

```text
E0 — hypothesis / suspicion / unverified agent claim
E1 — repo evidence: file:line, diff hunk, static search, config
E2 — command proof: tests, lint, typecheck, migration dry run, local script output
E3 — integration/runtime proof: local app, worker, scheduler, DB state, API path
E4 — deployed/live proof: deployed SHA verified + live tenant/user/system workflow verified
```

Treat uncited team claims as E0.

## Reconcile against reality

At the start of every orchestrator turn, check the available sources of truth:

1. Runtime/live system evidence when the question is deployed behavior.
2. PR/merge/branch state when the question is code shipping state.
3. Current repo files when the question is code state.
4. Task tracker/current roadmap when the question is assigned/planned state.
5. Memory/state docs when the question is recurring pattern/history.
6. Team sitrep text last, because it may be stale.

Use the project's actual commands. For GitHub projects, typical queries are:

```bash
# PRs merged since a date/window
gh pr list --state merged --search "merged:>=<YYYY-MM-DD>" \
  --json number,title,mergeCommit,headRefName,baseRefName,mergedAt,author

# Verify a cited PR
gh pr view <number> --json state,title,mergeCommit,headRefName,baseRefName,mergedAt,author,url

# Current branch and untracked work
git status --short
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
git log --oneline -n 10

# Compare branch ancestry
git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha_or_branch_a> <sha_or_branch_b>
```

For runtime claims, use environment-specific source-of-truth checks: deploy metadata, container image, release SHA, logs, DB reads, worker state, scheduler state, API responses, or live UI/API verification.

## Reconciliation script

```text
1. Read sitrep.
   - Extract dispatch IDs, task IDs, PR numbers, branches, commits, owner claims, evidence levels, blockers, and next actions.

2. Verify lineage.
   - Does the PR/branch/claim map to the expected DISPATCH_ID, bundle, owner, and plan lock?
   - Is PARENT_DISPATCH_ID consistent with the previous relay?

3. Verify each PR/branch claim.
   - Confirm state: open, merged, closed, draft.
   - Confirm title/description matches the claimed work.
   - Confirm merge commit/head branch/base branch.
   - Confirm whether sibling PRs landed in the same window.

4. Verify current repo/task/runtime state.
   - Check roadmap/status docs if used.
   - Check active task tracker.
   - Check memory/current coordination board.
   - Check git status for untracked docs or leftover work if local worktrees are involved.
   - Check deployed SHA/runtime state if the claim depends on deploy.

5. Identify drift.
   - Misattributed ownership.
   - Shipped work listed as parked/open.
   - Parked/deferred work listed as active.
   - Wrong PR number due to cross-repo collision.
   - Outside-scope work counted as orchestrated work.
   - Inferred runtime state stated as observed fact.
   - Local untracked plan/design docs omitted.
   - Missing boundary consumer or target entity proof.
   - Ceremony downgrade with no safety rationale.

6. Push back explicitly.
   - Restate the corrected fact with evidence.
   - Do not silently fix the team's state without telling it.

7. Update the orchestrator board/task tracker.
   - Reality beats sitrep.
   - File deferred follow-ups as separate tasks.
   - Merge/delete duplicates.

8. Respond with next step.
   - proceed, reroute, wait, serialize, dispatch audit, dispatch plan, dispatch impl, fold review, merge gate, live verify, defer, or human decision.
```

## Drift patterns to catch

### Misattributed ownership

A team may repeatedly attribute another team's work to the wrong owner. Always verify PR title, author/team mapping, branch naming, and known work sequence. Push back every time until the source corrects.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: <work item/PR> belongs to <actual owner>, not <claimed owner>. Evidence: <PR title/branch/merge commit/task board>. Please update your local state before the next sitrep.
```

### Shipped work listed as still parked/open

A team may list work as parked after it or a sibling already shipped it.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: this is no longer parked/open. It shipped as <PR/commit/date>. Next action should be <verify/fold/defer/close>, not implementation.
```

### Active work listed as shipped

A team may assume a PR merged or deployed when it only opened, merged to a working branch, or passed tests.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: current state is <open/merged-not-deployed/deployed-not-verified>. Merge/deploy/live verification are separate. Next gate is <gate>.
```

### Cross-repo or duplicate PR-number collisions

PR numbers can collide across repos. Never trust a bare number. Check repo prefix/title.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: <repo>#<number> is <title>. The cited work appears to be <other repo>#<number> or a different PR. Future sitreps should include repo prefix.
```

### Outside-scope work included in orchestrator totals

Parallel work by other sessions/workers can inflate shipped counts or confuse ownership.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: <PRs/work items> shipped during the window but were outside this orchestrated team. I am excluding them from this sprint/team state.
```

### Inferred runtime state treated as observed fact

Do not accept "the scheduler is stopped," "the worker is running," "the deploy picked it up," or "the migration succeeded" without checking the relevant runtime source.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: this was inferred, not observed. I need/ran <runtime check>. Observed state is <state>. Next action is <action>.
```

### Boundary contract missing or unproven

A team may claim a feature is done when it only wrote data, surfaced UI, or changed a staging object.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: boundary proof is incomplete. Current proof shows <writer/UI/staging>. Missing proof: <reader/downstream/canonical target>. Next gate is <audit/plan/fold/live verify>.
```

### Ceremony downgrade without rationale

A team may skip audit, review, or live verification because the task felt small.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: a ceremony downgrade occurred without a rationale. If the escalation scan is trigger-free, state why <skipped step> is safe; if any row is yes or unknown, use only the operator-waiver path or restore the default gate. Hard escalation triggers present: <none/list>.
```

### Untracked local docs/plans

Teams may leave local design/plan docs untracked after merge.

Response pattern:

```text
Housekeeping: untracked planning docs remain: <paths>. Either commit as approved docs, attach to the task, or delete if obsolete.
```

### Stale standing directives

A standing directive can become obsolete after a sibling team ships the dependency.

Response pattern:

```text
Correction: your standing directive is stale because <dependency> shipped as <PR/commit/date>. Replace next action with <new action>.
```

## Sitrep response format

When replying to a team sitrep, use this structure:

```text
ROLE: Orchestrator Planner
PHASE: RECONCILE
AUTHORITY: read-only
TASK_ID: <id>
DISPATCH_ID: <reconcile-dispatch-id>
PARENT_DISPATCH_ID: <incoming sitrep dispatch id>
EVIDENCE_TARGET: <E1 | E2 | E3 | E4>
FROM: <run>.orchestrator-planner
TO: <team>.planner | <team>.implementer | operator
CC: <run>.orchestrator-reviewer, <boundary-adjacent owner.role | none>
BUNDLE_ID: <bundle>
OWNER: <team/pair>
BASE: <repo>@<branch>@<sha or unknown>
TARGET_BRANCH: <branch or none>
DISPATCH_REQUIRED_FOR_IMPL: <yes/no>
HUMAN_GATE_REQUIRED: <yes — decision | no | no — downstream: merge requires human/operator gate>
LIVE_VERIFY_REQUIRED: <yes/no + reason>
CEREMONY_TIER: <tier>
CEREMONY_DOWNGRADE: <none or rationale>
FINAL_GIT_STATUS_SHORT: <paste exact output or unavailable — reason>

## Reconciled state
- <fact> — evidence level <E0-E4> — source: <source>

## Drift corrections
- <team claim> -> corrected to <truth> — evidence: <source>

## Boundary contract status
- <writes/reads/consumer/target/proof>

## Current blockers / collisions
- <blocker/collision/test/file/object>

## Task tracker updates
- <task -> state>

## Next action
- <dispatch audit | proceed to plan | dispatch impl | fold review | merge gate | live verify | defer | wait | human decision>

## Relay block, if needed
<paste full updated AUDIT/PLAN/IMPL/REVIEW-FOLD/SITREP/MERGE/LIVE block>
```

## Persistence rule

Some teams will repeat the same stale mislabel for multiple cycles. Do not assume one correction fixed it. Keep restating the truth with evidence each cycle until the team's sitrep self-corrects. Record recurring drift in memory or the orchestrator board.

## Do not do these

- Do not accept a sitrep as truth because it is confident.
- Do not route new work based on stale sibling state.
- Do not count outside-session work as this team's output.
- Do not trust bare PR numbers without repo/title.
- Do not confuse merged, deployed, and live-verified.
- Do not accept E2 tests as E4 live proof.
- Do not accept a writer without a reader or UI without a canonical target.
- Do not bury drift corrections in prose; make them explicit.
